# Fire Detection and Very Early Smoke Detection Apparatus (VESDA) {#sec-fire-detection-vesda}

## Aspiration Smoke Detection (ASD/VESDA): Laser detector units, sampling pipe runs, capillary drop tubes, and end-of-line test points

High-velocity airflows inside contained data halls (@sec-air-handling-containment) dilute incipient smoke plumes before they can trigger conventional ceiling point detectors [@nfpa75; @ref14_cxplanner]. Consequently, mission-critical white spaces, under-floor plenums, and return-air grilles deploy **Aspirating Smoke Detection ([ASD]{.gls} / [VESDA]{.gls})** systems (EN 54-20 Class A / NFPA 76 Very Early Warning Fire Detection), measured across the four life-safety packages in @tbl-fire-detection-vesda-boq [@nfpa75; @ref14_cxplanner].

| Life-Safety Detection Package | Primary Unit of Measurement | Standard Measurement Rules & Specifications | Critical QS Inclusions & Commissioning Drivers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Aspirating Smoke Detection (ASD / VESDA)** | Number (No.) of detectors + Linear Meter (m) of pipe | 1-pipe or 4-pipe laser chambers (EN 54-20 Class A); $25\text{ mm}$ OD halogen-free ABS/uPVC sampling pipework [@nfpa75; @rics2021nrm2]. | Dual-monitored 24V DC power supplies, capillary drop tubes, end-of-line test ports, and witnessed $\le 60\text{ s}$ smoke transport testing [@nfpa75; @ref14_cxplanner]. |
| **Cross-Zoned Addressable Point Detection** | Number (No.) by mounting horizon | Optical smoke, rate-of-rise thermal, and multi-criteria optical/thermal/CO detectors across under-floor, room, and ceiling voids [@nfpa75; @rics2021nrm2]. | Two independent coincidence loops required prior to gaseous discharge; remote LED indicators for concealed detectors [@sbc801_fire; @uae_fire_code]. |
| **Linear Heat Detection (LHD) Cabling** | Linear Meter (m) + Number (No.) of controllers | Digital or fiber-optic thermal sensing cable routed along MV/LV ladder racks and stationary battery frames [@rics2021nrm2; @ref04_helonic]. | Sinusoidal wave clipping length allowance over straight tray runs, end-of-line boxes, and distance-locating zone modules [@rics2021nrm2]. |
| **FACP, ARCP & Executive Action Relays** | Number (No.) of panels / monitored I/O modules | Networked Class A fault-tolerant loops in fire-resistant cable (BS 6387 Category CWZ) with monitored trip/status modules [@rics2021nrm2; @ref14_cxplanner]. | Cause-and-effect witness testing for fire dampers, CRAH/FCW trips, aisle drop-panels, mantrap fail-safe releases, and Civil Defense sign-off [@sbc801_fire; @uae_fire_code]. |

: Fire Detection, Aspirating Smoke Detection, and Alarm Control BOQ Breakdown {#tbl-fire-detection-vesda-boq}

Under RICS NRM2 Section 39 and CSI Division 28, ASD takeoff comprises:

- **Laser Aspirating Detector Panels (`No.`)**: 1-pipe or 4-pipe laser detection chambers complete with 24V DC dual-monitored power supplies, relay interface cards (Alert, Action, Fire 1, Fire 2), and Ethernet/Modbus monitoring [@rics2021nrm2; @ref14_cxplanner].
- **Halogen-Free ABS / uPVC Red Sampling Pipework (`m`)**: $25\text{ mm}$ OD air-sampling networks mounted along the ceiling grid, inside hot-aisle containment plenums, and directly across CRAH/FCW return-air faces [@ref14_cxplanner].
- **Capillary Drop Tubes & End-of-Line Test Ports (`No.`)**: Flexible capillary sampling tubes terminating in flush ceiling nozzles, plus accessible end-of-line smoke test ports for commissioning verification of the **60-second maximum transport time** [@nfpa75; @ref14_cxplanner].

## Multi-sensor intelligent addressable fire detection: Optical smoke, thermal, and carbon monoxide detectors in hot/cold aisles and ceiling plenums

In addition to VESDA, clean-agent releasing codes (@sec-fire-suppression-white-space; NFPA 72 / NFPA 2001 / SBC 801 / UAE Civil Defense) require **cross-zoned addressable point detection** (two independent detection loops or detector types in coincidence) before triggering gas release [@nfpa75; @sbc801_fire; @uae_fire_code]. Point detectors (optical smoke, rate-of-rise thermal, and multi-criteria optical/thermal/CO sensors for Li-ion battery off-gassing) are enumerated (`No.`) across three vertical horizons: (1) Under-floor void (if present), (2) Room/aisle level, and (3) Above-ceiling return plenum, complete with remote LED response indicators for concealed detectors [@rics2021nrm2; @ref14_cxplanner].

## Linear heat detection: Fiber-optic and digital sensor cables in cable trays and busway enclosures

To detect overheated joints or insulation breakdown along congested heavy-duty MV/LV cable ladder racks and battery racks, the MEP-QS measures **Digital or Fiber-Optic Linear Heat Detection ([LHD]{.gls}) Cable** in linear meters (`m`), clipped in a sinusoidal wave pattern along each tray tier, complete with zone controller modules, end-of-line termination boxes, and distance-locating [FACP]{.gls} integration [@rics2021nrm2; @ref04_helonic].

## Fire Alarm Control Panels (FACP) and voice evacuation: Executive action matrix mapping, HVAC trip relays, and fire damper release circuits

The life-safety network centers on peer-to-peer networked **Addressable Fire Alarm Control Panels (FACPs)** and **Agent Releasing Control Panels ([ARCPs]{.gls key="arcp"})** wired in Class A fault-tolerant redundant loops using fire-resistant cable (FP200 / MICC BS 6387 Category CWZ) [@rics2021nrm2; @ref14_cxplanner]. A major cost and commissioning driver is the **Cause-and-Effect (Executive Action) Matrix**: every motorized fire/smoke damper trip, CRAH/FCW fan shutdown relay, aisle containment drop-ceiling release electromagnet, access-control mantrap fail-safe unlock relay, and clean-agent abort/manual-release station must be individually measured, wired via monitored Input/Output (I/O) interface modules, and witness-tested during Level 4 FPT and Civil Defense inspection [@sbc801_fire; @uae_fire_code; @ref14_cxplanner].
